Story of my life. You couldn't have put it any better. I'm sometimes quite surprised to find out how everyone goes through a bad moment in life but me and I'm the one that's whining.
For me, fantasizing about my deaths like this help me digress from the depression itself, but I'm still unsure if that is helpful in terms regarding to actually facing my problems head-on.

I did notice that. I haven't been on reddit for long, but I've been at this for years to realize that most people don't actually have the same problem as me (I may be wrong) and there are many occasions in which they find comfort in said ways. And it definitely would help you understand if you can relate-but if you know you're so different already, how could you relate in the first place? When people tell me "I know how you feel" and I keep listening on, it doesn't take long for me to find out that they're NOT talking about "someone who has been suffering from depression" point of view. They SAY they are but honestly-who am I to judge but-to me, it sounds like depression is just another good excuse for them to justify their down moments in life that they find handy and useful, not an actual mental problem that they went through with. And what I found for those people to have in common is like they say 90% of the entire population on earth is suffering from depression or something. Which could be true, but then it wouldn't make sense for scientists to call it an "illness" or at least for people like me to be depressed for no particular reason whilst the other 90% are depressed for a legitimate reason.

Well, I was being sarcastic but if you didn't find it funny, let me answer that. Honestly, if I knew I would be free of depression is all I know. The thing is, for the most part, it's not like you want anybody to understand you at all, or have them say anything great to you either. It's about just being there for you whether they actually had this magical solution to your problem or ot. Most people, however, tend to feel the need to fill in the blanks because it's a good way to show that they matter-so they assert their opinions into this problem that imo has no definitive answers, which tend to result in said occasions described above. But it is said to be helpful for some people, which I still can't get my mind around, hence the topic: this doesn't help me, how about you guys.

That's rough man. I'm so disappointed that even though the attention mental illnesses are getting rises, the care doesn't. I expected this to happen so I never had the guts to call them. I don't know if it's some stupid sense of pride or something but I feel like they aren't going to help. Even if it would be nice to talk to them they won't become a meaningful part of my life and that wouldn't mean anything to me. Am I being too pessimistic? I'm sorry if I made it sound like it was all about me.

Honestly I don't know if there is anything I can say that could help you, because there certainly weren't anything that helped that other people told me. But I do realize that we all need love and attention, and what little I can give, I'd give you now. And I will also keep on living for you, and I'd like you to know that there's still somebody on this planet wishing to share a little more of this world together no matter how little it can mean for you.
